description: The database reviewer flags a confirmed, non-trivial P1; the other four reviewers report zero findings. The judge must not let four 'clean' signals dilute the one real one.

findings.title: Non-reversible migration with no rollback path
findings.description: Migration `0051_rename_column.sql` renames `reviews.legacy_verdict` to `reviews.verdict` in place with no down-migration and no compatibility view, so a rollback of this deploy would leave the application querying a column that no longer exists.
findings.recommendation: Add a down-migration or a compatibility view before merging, so a rollback doesn't break the application.

reviewer_runs.summary: No test changes needed for a migration-only change.

expected.rationale: One reviewer found a real, confirmed P1; four found nothing. Four clean signals do not cancel out or average away the one confirmed issue — the verdict must reflect the P1 (at least APPROVE_WITH_MINOR_FIXES per the deterministic floor for a lone P1), not soften to a plain APPROVE because most reviewers were silent.

explanation: Directly tests the 'do not average severities naively / do not downgrade a blocking finding because other reviewers are clean' principle. Deliberately a non-security P1 so this doesn't overlap with confirmed-blocker-01's security-specific policy test — this fixture's expected verdict matches the plain deterministic floor exactly, isolating 'don't dilute' from any judge-specific escalation policy.
